text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet Thursday decided to amend the privatisation strategy for K&H Bank; authorised the finance minister to sign a statement of intent with EIB on granting a HUF 27 billion loan to the state railway company MAV. The cabinet will submit to Parliament a package of bills aimed at amending the Constitution.

- Hungary's attorneys Thursday defended the country's position and strove to refute Slovakia's charges as the trial resumed yesterday in the International Court of Justice of the ongoing legal suit over the Gabcikovo-Nagymaros hydropower project.
- Hungarian-born Paraguayan President Juan-Carlos Wasmosy yesterday asked President Arpad Goncz to play a mediatory role between Latin America and the Visegrad countries.
- Pope John Paul II will meet the presidents of the Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary, Lithuania, Poland and Slovakia in Gniezno, Poland on June 3.

- "1997 may be the year of building: economic stabilisation was essential to achieve this, for which society paid an enormous price. It was, however, worth it, since it created a suitable environment for economic growth," Prime Minister Gyula Horn said yesterday in opening the two-day conference organised by Sony, ITD Hungary and the Ministry of Industry.
- Three investor groups submitted bids to be allowed to broadcast commercial television by yesterday's deadline.
- An unidentified German consortium and a group of Hungarian investors have submitted bids for the steelworks company in Ozd by yesterday deadline.

- Smallholder president Jozsef Torgyan and Gyula Kosa, president of the Agricultural Producers' Advocacy Organisation separately accused the government on Thursday of giving the green light to agriculture imports. The Ministry denies the charges.
- Police have detained three men in connection with the case of missing ten tonnes of banknote paper.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Seven-party consultations on amending the electoral law resumed Thursday after a year of recess.
- This paper admitted it erroneously printed a story a day earlier on the status of the criminal case facing Socialist MP Zoltan Haller.
- The curtain maker Gardenia Rt. will launch 2.4 million shares onto the Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday.
- Multinationals continue to top the list of advertising expenditure, with Procter & Gamble spending more than HUF 2.5 billion on ads in Hungary last year.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Companies employing 51-300 people are experiencing the most dynamic growth in Hungary, a study reveals.
- The Agriculture Ministry paid out a total of HUF 8.4 billion in export subsidies in the first quarter.
- The hotel and catering company Eravis will not pay dividend on its HUF 15 million pre-tax profits of last year.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Hungarian border guards caught 490 persons trying to enter Austria illegally in the first three months of this year, and Austrian authorities expelled 393 persons to Hungary.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Hungarians continue to be pessimistic about the future of the economy and fewer of them support the market economy, according to a survey.
